smells.finding: RealGateExtractor.fp_observations (fp_gate_real_extractor.py:363-439, ~77 lines) orchestrates session-load, apex/grip assembly, session-id lookup, latent extraction, driver->constructor remap, and RawFpObservation construction inline in one method. It already delegates the heavy lifting to extracted helpers (_apex_by_constructor, _representative_latent, per_car_grip_values), so this is a moderate orchestrator, not a raw blob — but it could still be split further (e.g. a private _observations_for_session helper) for readability. Not blocking for a thin, explicitly-illustrative demo module.

_ordered_drivers(db_path, year, weekend_id, session_type) is queried twice per FP session: once inside _apex_by_constructor (to build the apex pool) and again in fp_observations (to build drivers_by_constructor for the representative-latent lookup). Same query, same params, two round-trips. Minor inefficiency, not a correctness bug (demo is explicitly not optimized for statistical power/performance); worth a follow-up to pass the already-fetched driver list through instead of re-querying.
(year, gp, session_type) travels together as three separate positional/keyword params across _get_session_id, _ordered_drivers, _fastest_clean_lap rather than a bundled identity type.
